The user then approved page v2, verbatim via Optimize: "approved. proceed." v2 keeps storage order as it is (term order): a one-word key (atom, int, float, pid, ref) is found by word equality, as BEAM does, and order is consulted only to place a new key. Atom ids are not stable, so the v1 decisions on atom order are withdrawn. Page: https://claude.ai/artifact/MmnrdprbWQMF24ejqsUaQL (/Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-map-raw-words.html); measurements https://claude.ai/artifact/KASxGisqvtZNq498dbRi8D. User direction: meet or exceed BEAM in all cases; hand-written optimal arm64 first, then make the compiler emit it. Builder: Optimize. Pass rules are judged on bench and pre-registered on the page.

Step 1. Probes for get/fetch/has_key/replace/delete/update and their BEAM twins, checked in with a runner, with the numbers recorded. No runtime change.
- A 40-key build and lookup (the trie layout) are included.
- Hand-written arm64 sequences cover the scan-based put, binary-key lookup, replace and delete.

Local baselines (6 operations on a 12-key map, instructions, fz / BEAM):
- lookup, atom keys: 13,024 / 1,547
- lookup, binary keys: 20,484 / 6,460
- replace, atom: 7,342 / 2,918
- replace, binary: 9,565 / 7,701
- 3 deletes + 3 puts, atom: 17,638 / 3,735
- 3 deletes + 3 puts, binary: 24,252 / 13,240

Hand-written atom lookup: 367 per six.
title: Map lookup, replace and delete are measured against BEAM
